0.content: Alain Guillotin, called the "Lord-Artificer", was a Fontainian genius connected with the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. He built Marionette in the image of his dead younger sister, Mary-Ann, and activated her on his 65th birthday. When she first spoke, he regretted burdening her with his sister's life. He resolved she would choose her own name, birthday and path, and never again called her Marionette aloud. She found him messy ("Your life is a total mess"), then came to love him and called him a very good "father". He died in her care, telling her to seek her own desires. She wrote his epitaph using his favourite phrase, "Regrettably, there's nothing more to say", which he always said with a smile. She explains that he saw death as a silent equals sign, with himself moved to the other side.

key: Prospective Undulation Localized Observing and Investigating Automaton
1.content: Pulonia, the "Prospective Undulation Localized Observing and Investigating Automaton", was Alain's final creation: a huge automaton whose processing power went into simulating the future and calculating "the unknown". Alain gave it to Marionette as a companion; she taught it flowers and birds and looked after it like a baby brother. When she came home from Alain's funeral, too stunned to move, Pulonia held out its hand to her. She kept it rather than surrender it to the Fontaine Research Institute, quietly upgraded it, and fitted it for combat. Introducing it as her attendant kept curious eyes off Alain's secret.

key: Facilitatrice Automatisee Generaliste Interactive et Omnitache
2.content: Fagio, the "Facilitatrice Automatisee Generaliste Interactive et Omnitache", is the assistant automaton Sandrone built after her revival, designed to work with her Stellar Linchpin. Fagio handles trivial chores (whipping up dinner for unexpected guests, disposing of unwanted gifts, fetching tea leaves) and fights for her; she adapted Fagio's attack logic to the Linchpin's Cryo. When told the name is long and obscure, Sandrone is baffled. Alain named Pulonia the same way, and she wonders if the habit is hereditary.

3.content: When Columbina became a Harbinger she sang in the garden all day. She followed Sandrone everywhere, sang at her door at night, barged into her solo tea and took naps in her bed. Sandrone made her carry a heavy mainspring as punishment, and Columbina wore it for a week. She served her the nastiest drink she could, felt guilty when Columbina drank it, and gave her her precious tea snacks. Once she found Columbina crying in her sleep, covered her with a blanket and claimed Pulonia did it. She then lent Pulonia to sit with her in the garden. The next day Pulonia came to a meeting covered in flowers, and Columbina stood outside Sandrone's room wearing a sign calling herself a naughty child.

4.content: When Dottore seized the Three Moons' power, Sandrone built a world-formula to reconnect Columbina to Teyvat. She hid the real one in Pulonia and carried a fake. As Dottore moved to kill the Traveler she took the blow herself. Asked for last words, she thought of Alain asking what she wanted: she had always known what she did not want. She smiled and told Dottore to go to hell. He killed her, but the formula ran on and Columbina returned to destroy him. Per her old verbal will, Arlecchino sent her and Pulonia's cores to the Fontaine Research Institute.

5.content: Dottore, the Second Harbinger, is the colleague Sandrone hates above all. Asked about him, she warns you to cover your ears. She resented that his projects were funded ten times faster than hers and suspected Pantalone of favouring him. In Nod-Krai she thought him incapable of human interaction. When he went quiet she grew suspicious, and she was disgusted to find him turning her own subordinates into monsters. He noted that her new concern for others was out of character, and in the final battle he mocked her inability to trust.
